# Local Image Analysis

Two rules, in order.

1. **First, find out if this model has vision.** Call `read(<path>)` on the
   image file.
2. **Then act on the result.**
   - You have vision if the `read(...)` result lets you actually perceive the
     picture (the image appears in your context and you can describe its
     contents).
   - You do **not** have vision if `read(...)` returns no perceivable image
     content, errors out, or the harness tells you image attachments are not
     supported for this model.

## Rule 1 — You have vision

Analyze the image directly from what `read(...)` gave you. Do not call the
gateway. Report your findings in your answer. Stop.

## Rule 2 — You have no vision (delegate to Gemma 4 26B)

Do **not** describe the image from guesswork, from the filename, or from a
previous context. The model cannot see the image; only the instructions below
can produce a trustworthy description.

Send the image to the local Gemma 4 26B vision model through the llama-swap
gateway (OpenAI-compatible endpoint on this machine).

**You can ask the image model anything about the picture** — description,
transcription/OCR, layout, objects, people, colors, text, style, defects,
artifacts, or any other question the user asked. Pass the user's real question
to the model as a clear, focused instruction. Do not invent or guess the
answer yourself when you have no vision; the image model is the source of
truth.

### Recipe — one exact curl

The gateway is already running at `http://127.0.0.1:8080` (llama-swap).
Do not start or stop it. Model id (exact string): `gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat-q4k-xl`.

Copy this exact command and change only `/path/to/file.png` and the prompt
text. It sends the image, runs the analysis, and prints the answer. Replace
the `--arg p '...'` prompt string with the user's actual question about the
image — any question is valid.

```bash
jq -n --arg p 'Describe this image in detail. Transcribe any visible text exactly.' \
  --rawfile b <(base64 -w0 /path/to/file.png) \
  '{model:"gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat-q4k-xl",messages:[{role:"user",content:[{type:"text",text:$p},{type:"image_url",image_url:{url:("data:image/png;base64,"+$b)}}]}],reasoning_effort:"max"}' \
  | curl -s --max-time 300 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @- \
    http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/co
